info.name: PhotoCraft AI - Kiosk API
info.description:
Endpoints called by the on-site photo Kiosk / booth terminal (photographer capture & upload, AI face match against the day's uploads, product/frame selection, cart, checkout and order management at the counter).

Backend: `graspcraft_laravel` (Laravel port of `graspcraft_backend` NestJS API). Base path is `/api` (see `bootstrap/app.php`).

**Auth note:** `JwtMiddleware` exists but is **not currently registered** in `bootstrap/app.php`, so every endpoint is unauthenticated today. This collection still sends `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` on every request except Login, so it keeps working the moment auth is turned on.

**Response envelope:** every JSON endpoint (except the pre-signed image URL's redirect target and the ZIP download) replies
```
{ "code": number, "status": boolean, "msg": string, "data": any }
```
A business failure (bad password, missing record, etc.) is **not** an HTTP error - it comes back with a 200/201 status and `status: false`. Always branch on the body's `status`, not the HTTP status.

Routes here were confirmed against the controllers/services (not just route names) - see the per-request description for the code reference and any quirks.

request.description:
`UsersController::userLogin` -> `UsersService::userLogin`.

Required: `username`, `password`. `type` selects the table: any value other than `"customer"` is looked up against `users` (kiosk/photographer/staff/admin accounts); `type: "customer"` looks up `customers`.

The password is matched by deterministic-cipher equality, not bcrypt. On success the row is returned with an extra `token` (HS256 JWT, 1-day expiry, same secret/claims as the Node app) grafted onto `data.token`. On a bad username/password the envelope comes back `status: false` with a 201 HTTP status (this is a POST route) - it is NOT a 401.

This is the one route excluded from `JwtMiddleware` once auth is enabled.

exec: pm.test('login response has a body', function () {

request.description: `UsersController::userLogout`. Stateless no-op server-side (there is no session/token blocklist) - the client is expected to discard its own `token`. Always returns `status: true`.

`UsersController::customerRegistor` -> `UsersService::customerRegistor`. Creates a row in `customers`. Path is spelled `customer-registor` in the live route table - that is not a typo in this collection, it is what the API actually exposes.

Required for a usable account: `user_name`, `email_id`, `password`. `name`, `ph_number`, `customer_code`, `role_id` are accepted but optional. Uniqueness is checked on `user_name` + `email_id` together; a duplicate throws and the envelope comes back `status: false`. `password` is encrypted before storage - it is the only encrypted column on `customers`.

No server-side field validation beyond that (this route takes the raw request body, unlike the Admin master-data routes which use typed FormRequests).

`UsersController::checkExistUser` -> `UsersService::checkExistUser`. Required: `user_name`, `email_id` (both, exact match against `users`). Returns the matching row's `id` on success; when no row matches it throws and the envelope carries `status: false` with the message "User does'nt exist...!" (exact wording from the source).

Note: `email_id` is compared as plaintext against the encrypted column, so this only ever matches rows whose email was stored before encryption was introduced - a known, reproduced quirk, not something to 'fix' in a test.

`PguserController::uploads3` -> `PguserService::uploads3`. Path segment `image` is `uploadtype` (path param, not query) - it selects the S3 bucket and whether an `images_upload` row is written. Other values (`frame`, `product`, `combo`, `ads`, `framedImages`, `object`, `ultraObject`) exist on the same route but are Web/admin master-data upload flows, out of scope for this collection - `image` is the one the kiosk capture screen actually uses.

`pguser_id` query param is required - the logged-in kiosk/photographer's user id. `files` (multipart, one or more) is required - Rekognition indexing happens against these on upload. `photoToFrameMap` is a JSON-string form field, only read when uploadtype is `framedImages`.

On a partial failure the response still comes back 201 but with an `error` key inside `data` - check for that, not just the envelope `status`.

formdata.description: One or more captured photo files (repeat the 'files' key per file).
Second file, optional - shows the multi-file shape.
JSON string, only used when uploadtype is 'framedImages'. Leave empty for a plain capture upload (uploadtype=image).

request.description: `PguserController::dashboard` -> `PguserService::dashboard`. Path param `pguser_id` (required). Returns lifetime and today's upload counts for this kiosk/photographer, e.g. `[{ "total_count": "42", "today_count": "5" }]` (counts are returned as strings - Postgres bigint aggregates).

`PguserController::getHistory` -> `PguserService::getHistory`. Path param `pguser_id` (required). One row per upload batch (grouped by time/date/created_at), newest first - lets the kiosk show 'sessions uploaded today'.

`PguserController::saveEditedFrame` -> `PguserService::saveEditedFrame`. Path param `frame_img_id` (a `fram_img_map.id`, required). Multipart `file` is required. Uploads the retouched image, marks the fram-img-map row `is_edited = true`, and returns a pre-signed URL so the kiosk can show the result immediately.

Handled failures (`file` missing, or `frame_img_id` not found) come back as `status: false` with a specific message rather than the generic error - useful to assert on directly.

item.name: Compare Face Against Today's Uploads (AI Match)

request.description:
`UsersController::compareUserFaces` -> `UsersService::compareImages`. This is the AI/Rekognition face-match step (documented in the service as the kiosk's face match): sends `file` to AWS Rekognition and matches it against the requested date/time window of `images_upload` rows.

Behaviour to test for:
- No active frame configured -> `status:false`, message is the 'no active frame' notice.
- `file` omitted, or Rekognition finds no match -> falls back to returning every upload in the requested date/time window instead (`comparedImages`, `unmatchedFaces: true`).
- A genuine match -> `{ frames: [...], comparedImages: [...], unmatchedFaces: false }`.

`photoFrameRequest` fields are read from a JSON **string**, not nested JSON - keep it as a form-data text field, not a nested object.

formdata.description: Required to actually run a face match. The captured/selfie photo.
JSON string. date=dd-mm-yyyy (required for the date filter to apply); from_time/to_time are 'hh:mm AM/PM' strings, optional.

request.description: `UsersController::getCustomerImages` -> `UsersService::customerImages`. Required: `customer_id`. `page_no`/`limit` optional (default 1/10). Returns `{ count, rows }` from `images_upload` where `customer_id` matches.

`UsersController::deleteCustomerImages` -> `UsersService::deleteCustomerImages`. Required: `ids` (array of `images_upload.id`). This is a HARD delete (`forceDelete`), not a soft delete - there is no undo.

item.name: Get Product/Combo Screen + My Framed Photos

request.description:
`UsersController::getFrameWithImages` -> `UsersService::getFrameWithImages`. Path param `customer_id` (required). Documented in the source as 'the kiosk's product screen': every active combo with its products, plus the frame images already composed for this customer (`fram_img_map` rows).

Returns `status:false` (EM014) when no combo is configured at all - that is a real, testable state, not just an edge case.

`UsersController::updateCustomer` -> `UsersService::updateCustomer`. Path param `customer_id` (required). `role_id` in the body is required and must resolve to an existing staff `users` row (this is how the operator attributes a customer to the staff member checking them in) - an unresolvable `role_id` returns `status:false` (EM017), a real 'wrong ID' state worth testing, not a 404.

Any other `customers` column (`name`, `ph_number`, `email_id`, `customer_code`) can be included and is written through as-is.

`AppController::downloadFramedImg`. Path param is the stored S3 key/filename (e.g. an `img_url`/`merged_img_name`/`edited_img_name` value from an earlier response) - replace `edited_12345678.jpg` with a real key. Returns a pre-signed download URL in `data`, not the binary image itself.

item.name: Get Emailed Images For an Order

request.description:
`UsersController::emailedImages` -> `UsersService::getEmailedImages`. Required: `order_id` (the `orders.order_id` string), `customer_id`. Returns the file names of the order's 'email' product images.

Side effect worth knowing before you re-run this in a test: it bumps `orders.print_count` and rewrites the customer's stored `name`/`email_id` from the order snapshot every time it's called.

`UsersController::downloadImagesZip`. Required: `order_id`. **This route does not use the standard envelope**: on success it streams a binary `application/zip` file directly (use Postman's "Save Response > Save to a file"); when the order has no emailed images it answers a bare 404 JSON `{ status: false, msg: "No images found for this order" }`.

`CartController::create` -> `CartService::create`. Required: `customer_id`, `combo_id`, `combo_map` (the whole basket-line snapshot - `combo_map` is written into the stored `combo_json` column). `product_list[].product_type` drives how images are resolved later (`magnet`, a certificate type, or the default frame lookup via `frame_img_ids`). `qty` optional (defaults handled by the column default).
`CartController::findAll` -> `CartService::findAll`. Path param `customer_id` (required). Every cart row for this customer, with the combo/products resolved and each product's `framedNames` attached.
`CartController::remove` -> `CartService::deleteOneCart`. Path param `cart_id` (required). Hard delete of one `cart` row.

`CartController::removeMultiple` -> `CartService::deleteMultipleCart`. Path param `customer_id` (required). Hard-deletes every cart row for this customer - this is what clears the basket right after checkout.

`CartController::getOneOrder` -> `CartService::getOneOrder`. Path param `order_id` (the `orders.order_id` string, required). Returns the order with its basket, where every `frame_img_ids` array has been replaced with resolved `frame_img_names` - built for a receipt/confirmation screen. Throws (`status:false`) when the order does not exist.

`DiscountController::findAmount` -> `DiscountService::findAmount`. Path param is the discount code the customer typed in (required). An unknown code returns `status:false` (EM018) rather than a 404 - assert on the body, not the HTTP status.

`UsersController::createOrder` -> `UsersService::createOrder`. `customer_id` and `amount` are the practical minimum; `date`, `time` and `order_id` are generated server-side and do not need to be sent. `payment_type` is one of `card`/`cash`/`qr`. `order_status` is one of `pending`/`failed`/`cancelled`/`completed` (`pending` is typical at creation).

`staff_code` is optional, but if supplied it must resolve to an active staff member - an unresolvable code throws a **dedicated 400** (`ER002`) carrying the exact message, so the client can show it verbatim. That is the one route in this collection where a failure IS a real HTTP error, not just `status:false`.

Response includes a `sendMail` flag telling the caller whether this order contains an emailed product (drives a 'we'll email your photos' prompt).

`UsersController::updateOrder` -> `UsersService::updateOrder`. Path param `order_id` (the `orders.order_id` string; note this is not unique, so the update can touch more than one row). Any `orders` column can be sent; `order_status` is the meaningful one - transitioning to `completed` accrues staff commission (once, guarded against double-accrual), transitioning to `cancelled`/`failed` reverses pending commission.

`UsersController::findAllOrders` -> `UsersService::findAllOrders`. `user_type` is **required**. `from_date`/`to_date` have an odd, deliberately-reproduced validation quirk: omitting BOTH is fine, sending only one of them fails validation - if you use date filtering, always send both (empty string is accepted).

When `logined_userId` is set and `user_type` is not one of the admin-tier types, results are scoped to the kiosks that operator's role grants (`role_kiosk_map`) - this is what makes the endpoint kiosk-operator-safe to expose (an operator only ever sees their own kiosk's orders). Returns `{ count, rows, total_amount }` - `total_amount` is summed across the whole filtered set, not just the current page.

`UsersController::findOneOrder` -> `UsersService::findOneOrder`. Path param is the `orders.id` primary key (not the `order_id` string used by the cart/checkout routes above) - required. Returns the order with its kiosk `user` relation resolved to `{id, name}`.
